q: Around _____ of 118 elements in the Periodic Table are classified as metals.
e: Around 95 of 118 elements in the Periodic Table are classified as metals.

q: The reactivity series of metals is a series in which metals are arranged in order of reactivity from _____.
e: The reactivity series of metals is a series in which metals are arranged in order of reactivity from highest to lowest.

q: Metals above carbon can only be extracted from their ores by _____.
e: Metals above carbon can only be extracted from their ores by electrolysis.

q: Metals below hydrogen can neither be reacted with water nor acid, and cannot easily be _____.
e: Metals below hydrogen can neither be reacted with water nor acid, and cannot easily be tarnished or corroded.

q: Potassium and sodium must be stored in _____ to avoid exposing them to moisture and oxygen in the air.
e: Potassium and sodium must be stored in kerosene to avoid exposing them to moisture and oxygen in the air.

q: Some metals such as iron, copper, zinc, and nickel are slower to oxidise because they form a _____ layer of oxide that protects the interior.
e: Some metals are slower to oxidise because they form a passive layer of oxide that protects the interior.

q: Reactive metals such as potassium, sodium and calcium react with cold water to produce the metal hydroxide and _____ gas.
e: Reactive metals react with cold water to produce the metal hydroxide and hydrogen gas.

q: Moderately reactive metals such as magnesium, zinc and iron react more rapidly with steam to form metal oxide and _____.
e: Moderately reactive metals react more rapidly with steam to form metal oxide and hydrogen.

q: The reactions of metals with dilute acids ($HCl$ and $H_2SO_4$) produce the corresponding metallic salts and _____ gas.
e: The reactions of metals with dilute acids produce the corresponding metallic salts and hydrogen gas.

q: Displacement reaction is a chemical reaction in which a _____ metal displaces a less reactive metal from its compound.
e: Displacement reaction is a chemical reaction in which a more reactive metal displaces a less reactive metal from its compound.

q: In the displacement reaction between a metal and metal oxide, the more reactive metal will take the _____ atom from the less reactive metal oxide.
e: In the displacement reaction between a metal and metal oxide, the more reactive metal will take the oxygen atom from the less reactive metal oxide.

q: The Reactivity Series of metals is the arrangement of metals in the _____ order of reactivity.
e: The Reactivity Series of metals is the arrangement of metals in the decreasing order of reactivity.

q: The more reactive metals are easy to lose electrons and form _____ ions.
e: The more reactive metals are easy to lose electrons and form positive ions.

q: Potassium burns vigorously with a bright _____ flame.
e: Potassium burns vigorously with a bright lilac flame.

q: Sodium burns vigorously with a bright _____ flame.
e: Sodium burns vigorously with a bright yellow flame.

q: Calcium burns quickly with a bright _____ flame.
e: Calcium burns quickly with a bright orange-red flame.

q: Magnesium burns quickly with a bright _____ flame.
e: Magnesium burns quickly with a bright white flame.

q: Aluminium burns quickly with a bright _____ flame.
e: Aluminium burns quickly with a bright yellow flame.

q: Zinc burns quickly with a _____ flame.
e: Zinc burns quickly with a light blue flame.

q: Iron burns quickly with _____.
e: Iron burns quickly with yellow sparks.

q: Tin, lead, copper, and mercury react _____ even at high temperature.
e: Tin, lead, copper, and mercury react slowly even at high temperature.

q: Silver, gold, and platinum show _____ reaction with oxygen.
e: Silver, gold, and platinum show no reaction with oxygen.

q: Potassium and sodium react _____ with cold water, float, and catch fire.
e: Potassium and sodium react violently with cold water, float, and catch fire.

q: Magnesium reacts very slowly with cold water, but _____ with steam.
e: Magnesium reacts very slowly with cold water, but vigorously with steam.

q: Lead reacts _____ with hydrochloric acid, either dilute or concentrated.
e: Lead reacts very slowly with hydrochloric acid, either dilute or concentrated.

q: _____ are those minerals from which metals are extracted economically.
e: Ores are those minerals from which metals are extracted economically.

q: The process of extracting a metal from its ore is called _____.
e: The process of extracting a metal from its ore is called metallurgy.

q: The three major steps of extracting metal from its ore are concentration of the ore, _____ of the metal, and purification of the metal.
e: The three major steps are concentration of the ore, isolation of the metal, and purification of the metal.

q: Removal of unwanted materials from the ore is known as concentration or _____.
e: Removal of unwanted materials from the ore is known as concentration or dressing.

q: Gravity separation is based on the difference in _____ of metal ores and that of clay, sand, stone, and limestone.
e: Gravity separation is based on the difference in specific gravity of metal ores and impurities.

q: Froth flotation process is generally used to concentrate the _____ ores.
e: Froth flotation process is generally used to concentrate the sulphide ores.

q: In froth flotation process, _____ ores get wet easily with oil.
e: In froth flotation process, sulphide ores get wet easily with oil.

q: Magnetic separation is based on differences in the _____ properties of the ore components.
e: Magnetic separation is based on differences in the magnetic properties of the ore components.

q: In the chemical process of concentration, the desired minerals of the ores are _____ in a particular solution.
e: In the chemical process, the desired minerals of the ores are dissolved in a particular solution.

q: Calcination involves heating when the _____ matter escapes leaving behind the metal oxide.
e: Calcination involves heating when the volatile matter escapes leaving behind the metal oxide.

q: In calcination, the concentrated ores are heated at a temperature below the melting point in the _____ of air.
e: In calcination, the concentrated ores are heated at a temperature below the melting point in the absence of air.

q: In roasting, the ore is heated in a regular supply of air in a furnace at a temperature _____ the melting point of the metal.
e: In roasting, the ore is heated in a regular supply of air in a furnace at a temperature below the melting point of the metal.

q: Generally, roasting is applied for _____ ores.
e: Generally roasting is applied for sulphide ores.

q: Which of the following is NOT a main reduction method of metal oxide?
e: The three main reduction methods are reduction with carbon, reduction by electrolysis, and reduction with a more reactive metal.

q: _____ is added to the ores to remove mineral impurities during purification.
e: Flux is added to the ores to remove mineral impurities.

q: Flux joins with impurities and forms _____.
e: Flux joins with impurities and forms metal slag.

q: The process in which flux joins with impurities to form metal slag that can be easily removed from molten metal is called _____.
e: This process is called smelting.

q: Purification by _____ is done to make the metal more pure than that obtained in the smelting process.
e: Purification by electrolysis is done to make the metal becomes more pure than that obtained in the smelting process.

q: _____ is the earthy impurities (sand, silt, gravel, etc.) associated with the ore.
e: Gangue is the earthy impurities associated with the ore.

q: Froth flotation selectively separates materials based upon whether they are water repelling (_____) or have an affinity for water (hydrophilic).
e: Froth flotation selectively separates materials based upon whether they are water repelling (hydrophobic) or have an affinity for water (hydrophilic).

q: In froth flotation, the mineral impurities (gangue) settle at the _____ of the bowl as residues.
e: The mineral impurities (gangue) settle at the bottom of the bowl as residues.

q: During magnetic separation, crushed ores are passed through a plastic conveyor belt where the outer wheel has a _____ property.
e: The outer wheel of the conveyor belt has a magnetic property.

q: Oxides are easier to _____, so the concentrated ore is usually converted to an oxide before reduction.
e: Oxides are easier to reduce. Thus, isolation of metals from concentrated ore involves conversion to oxide before reduction.

q: In the chemical process of concentration, the mineral impurities are removed by _____.
e: The mineral impurities are separated and removed by filtration.

q: Metallurgy is the process used for the extraction of _____ metals from their ores.
e: Metallurgy is the process used for the extraction of pure metals from their ores.

q: In Myanmar, copper and _____ are rich mineral resources, and iron is a fairly rich resource.
e: In Myanmar, copper and lead are rich mineral resources, and iron is a fairly rich resource.

q: Iron ore deposits in Myanmar are commonly found in Northern Shan State and in _____ State.
e: Iron ore deposits are commonly found in Northern Shan State and in Kachin State.

q: If a metal is less reactive than carbon, it can be extracted from its oxide by heating with _____ as a reducing agent.
e: If a metal is less reactive than carbon, it can be extracted from its oxide by heating with carbon as a reducing agent.

q: The aluminium ore _____ is treated with sodium hydroxide to obtain pure alumina.
e: Aluminium ore bauxite is treated with sodium hydroxide to obtain pure alumina.

q: Molten _____ is added to dissolve alumina because it has a lower melting point than alumina and can reduce the temperature of fusion.
e: Molten cryolite is added into the container to dissolve the alumina because cryolite has a lower melting point than alumina.

q: In the electrolysis for the extraction of aluminium, aluminium is produced at the _____ and oxygen is liberated at the anode.
e: Aluminium is produced at the cathode and oxygen is liberated at the anode.

q: Aluminium is a silvery-white metal that is very _____ and malleable.
e: Aluminium is a silvery-white metal. It is very ductile and malleable.

q: In moist air, a film of _____ is formed on the aluminium surface which prevents any further attack on the underlying metal.
e: In moist air, a film of oxide is formed on the metal surface which prevents any further attack on the underlying metal.

q: The melting point of aluminium is _____.
e: The melting point of aluminium is $660^{\circ} C$.

q: Since aluminium can react with alkalis as well as with acids, it is an _____ metal.
e: Since aluminium can react with alkalis as well as with acids, it is an amphoteric metal.

q: The reduction of the metallic oxide with aluminium is known as the _____ reaction.
e: The reduction of the metallic oxide with aluminium is known as the Thermite reaction.

q: Haematite ($Fe_2O_3$) and _____ ($Fe_3O_4$) ores are suitable for the extraction of iron.
e: Haematite ($Fe_2O_3$) and magnetite ($Fe_3O_4$) ores are suitable for the extraction of iron.

q: The extraction of iron is carried out in the _____ because a lot of heat is required.
e: The reaction is carried out in the blast furnace because a lot of heat is required.

q: In the blast furnace, coke burns to produce _____.
e: The coke burns to produce carbon dioxide.

q: The $CO_2$ produced in the blast furnace reacts with more carbon to form _____.
e: The $CO_2$ produced reacts with more carbon to form carbon monoxide.

q: The _____ formed in the blast furnace reduces the oxides of iron to iron.
e: The CO formed reduces the oxides of iron to iron.

q: In the blast furnace, limestone ($CaCO_3$) breaks down due to heat to form calcium oxide and _____.
e: Limestone ($CaCO_3$) breaks down due to the heat of the furnace to form calcium oxide and carbon dioxide.

q: Calcium oxide reacts with sand (silicon dioxide) to form _____ (slag) which floats on the molten iron.
e: Calcium oxide reacts with the sand (silicon dioxide or silica) to form calcium silicate (slag).

q: The iron obtained from the blast furnace is known as pig or cast iron and contains about _____% carbon.
e: The iron obtained by this process is known as pig or cast iron and contains about 4% carbon.

q: Pure iron is soft and malleable, and unlike most other metals, it is _____.
e: Pure iron is soft and malleable. Unlike most other metals, it is magnetic.

q: The melting point of pure iron is _____.
e: The melting point of pure iron is $1538^{\circ} C$.

q: When chlorine passes over heated iron, iron is oxidised to _____.
e: When chlorine passes over heated iron, iron is oxidised to iron(III) chloride.

q: Iron reacts with dilute sulphuric acid to form _____ and hydrogen.
e: Iron reacts with dilute sulphuric acid to form iron(II) sulphate and hydrogen.

q: The lead ore _____ (PbS) is ground into small particles for extraction.
e: The lead ore, galena (PbS), is ground into small particles.

q: The lead powder is put through a _____ process to form oil froth containing lead ore.
e: The lead powder is put through a flotation process.

q: In lead extraction, the powder is heated to more than _____ producing lead(II) oxide and volatile sulphur dioxide.
e: The powder is then heated to more than $1370^{\circ} C$ producing lead(II) oxide and volatile sulphur dioxide.

q: Lead is a _____-grey metal and is the softest of the metals in common use.
e: Lead is a bluish-grey metal. It is the softest of the metals in common use.

q: On exposure to air, lead is tarnished owing to the formation of a layer of hydroxide and _____ which prevents further attack.
e: On exposure to air, lead is tarnished owing to the formation of a layer of hydroxide and carbonate.

q: Lead has a low melting point of _____.
e: Lead has a low melting point ($328^{\circ} C$).

q: Lead does not react with _____ or steam.
e: Lead does not react with water or steam.

q: The main source of copper ore is copper pyrites, also known as _____.
e: The main source of copper ore is copper pyrites (also known as chalcopyrite), $CuFeS_2$.

q: The concentrated copper ore is heated strongly with _____ (silica) and air or oxygen in a furnace.
e: The concentrated ore is heated strongly with silicon dioxide (silica) and air or oxygen in a furnace.

q: In the extraction of copper, the copper in copper pyrites is reduced to _____.
e: The copper in the copper pyrites is reduced to copper(I) sulphide.

q: In copper extraction, the iron in copper pyrites is converted into an _____ slag which is removed.
e: The iron in the copper pyrites is converted into an iron(II) silicate slag which is removed.

q: Most of the sulphur in copper pyrites turns into _____ gas during extraction.
e: Most of the sulphur in the copper pyrites turns into sulphur dioxide gas.

q: The end product of copper extraction before electrolytic refining is _____ copper, which is about 98~99.5% pure.
e: The end product, blister copper, is a porous brittle form of copper which is about 98~99.5% pure.

q: A freshly exposed surface of pure copper has a _____ colour.
e: A freshly exposed surface of pure copper has a pinkish-orange colour.

q: The melting point of copper is _____.
e: The melting point of copper is $1084^{\circ} C$.

q: In a pure metal, atoms are packed regularly in layers that can _____ over one another when force is applied.
e: In a pure metal, atoms are packed regularly in layers. These layers of atoms can slide over one another when force is applied.

q: When a pure metal is alloyed, atoms of the added element have _____ sizes from those of the pure metal.
e: When a pure metal is alloyed, atoms of the added element have different sizes from those of the pure metal.

q: The atoms of different sizes cannot slide over each other easily, and this makes the alloy _____ than the pure metals.
e: The atoms of different sizes cannot slide over each other easily and this makes the alloy harder than the pure metals.

q: Alloying can be used to improve the appearance and _____ of the metal.
e: Alloying can also be used to improve the appearance and properties of the metal.

q: Mixing molten tin and copper gives a gold-coloured alloy called _____.
e: Mixing molten tin and copper gives a gold-coloured alloy called bronze.

q: The resulting bronze will have much greater strength, hardness and _____ resistance.
e: The resulting bronze will have much greater strength, hardness and corrosion resistance.

q: Steel is an alloy of iron containing _____ and other metals.
e: Steel is an alloy of iron containing carbon and other metals.

q: Cupronickel is an alloy containing 75% Cu and 25% Ni, and it is commonly used for making _____.
e: Cupronickel has special properties of being hard, shining and lasting, and is used for coins.

q: Brass is an alloy containing 70% Cu and 30% Zn, and it does not _____ easily.
e: Brass does not corrode easily and is used for ship boilers.

q: Bronze contains 90% Cu and 10% Sn, and it is used for making _____.
e: Bronze is very hard and strong, and is used for ship propellers.

q: Solder contains 70% Pb and 30% Sn, and its special property is a _____ melting point.
e: Solder has a low melting point and is used for soldering wires.

q: Duralumin is an alloy of aluminium that is light and strong, making it suitable for the body of an _____.
e: Duralumin is light and strong, used for the body of an aeroplane and bullet train.

q: Magnalium contains 70% Al and 30% Mg, and its special properties are hard but _____.
e: Magnalium is hard but light, used for aircraft structure.

q: Pink gold contains 75% Au, 20% Cu, and 5% Ag, and it is used for making _____.
e: Pink gold is soft, malleable, ductile, and used for gold jewellery.

q: Mild steel contains 99.7% Fe and 0.3% C, and it is used for car bodies, building, ship and _____.
e: Mild steel is hard and strong, used for car bodies, building, ship and machinery.

q: Hard steel contains 99% Fe and 1% C, and it is hard and _____.
e: Hard steel is hard and brittle, used for cutting tools, razor blades, chisels.

q: Soft steel contains 99.8% Fe and 0.2% C, and its special properties are malleable and _____.
e: Soft steel is malleable and ductile, used for cable, nail, chain.

q: Stainless steel is an alloy that is hard and _____.
e: Stainless steel is hard and rustproof, used for cutlery and surgical instruments.

q: Nickel steel is hard, elastic and _____, making it useful for cable, automobile and aeroplane parts.
e: Nickel steel is hard, elastic and rustproof.

q: Tungsten steel is hard and has resistance to _____, making it suitable for high speed cutting tools and springs.
e: Tungsten steel is hard and has resistance to corrosion.

q: Manganese steel is extremely hard and has a high _____ point, making it suitable for rail tracks and rock crushers.
e: Manganese steel is extremely hard and has a high melting point.

q: An _____ is a mixture of metals with other elements, especially to give greater strength or resistance to corrosion.
e: An alloy is a mixture of metals with other elements, especially to give greater strength or resistance to corrosion.

q: Steel is a mixture of the metal iron and the non-metal _____.
e: Steel is a mixture of the metal iron and the non-metal carbon.

q: Traces of sulphur, phosphorus and silicon are added as _____ of alloys.
e: Traces of sulphur, phosphorus and silicon are added as modifiers of alloys.

q: The percentage of metals to make alloy has been varied for _____ applications.
e: The percentage of metals to make alloy has been varied for particular applications.

q: Corrosion is the deterioration of metals as a result of _____ reaction depending on the type of metal and the environmental conditions.
e: Corrosion is the deterioration of metals as a result of chemical reaction depending on the type of metal and the environmental conditions.

q: Corrosion of iron is specifically called _____.
e: Corrosion of iron is called rusting.

q: Most metals, except _____, can be corroded because they oxidise.
e: Most metals, except gold, can be corroded because they oxidise.

q: Silver reacts with sulphur in the air to form silver sulphide ($Ag_2S$), and turns _____.
e: Silver reacts with sulphur in the air to form silver sulphide ($Ag_2S$), and turns black.

q: Copper reacts with moist carbon dioxide in the air and gets a green coat called _____.
e: Copper reacts with moist carbon dioxide in the air and gets a green coat called verdigris.

q: Iron acquires a coating of a brown flaky substance called _____ ($Fe_2O_3 \cdot xH_2O$).
e: Iron acquires a coating of a brown flaky substance called rust.

q: Both _____ and moisture are necessary for the rusting of iron.
e: Both air and moisture are necessary for rusting of iron.

q: Plating, painting, oiling or greasing, and making alloy are commonly used to protect a metal from _____.
e: Plating, painting, oiling or greasing and making alloy are commonly used to protect a metal from corrosion.

q: Chrome plating is a method of applying a thin layer of _____ onto a metal object.
e: Chrome plating (chromium plating) process is a method of applying a thin layer of chromium onto a metal object.

q: The chromed layer is decorative, and provides _____ resistance.
e: The chromed layer is decorative, and provides corrosion resistance.

q: Tin plating is commonly used in making _____.
e: Tin plating is commonly used in making food cans.

q: Galvanising is the process of immersing iron or steel in molten _____.
e: Galvanising is the process of immersing iron or steel in molten zinc.

q: Galvanising is used to protect iron exposed to a non-corrosive medium such as _____.
e: Galvanising is used to protect iron exposed to non-corrosive medium (air).

q: Sacrificial protection is used to protect iron exposed to a corrosive medium by attaching a _____ bar to iron or steel.
e: In sacrificial protection, a zinc bar is attached to iron or steel.

q: The main stages of metal recycling are collection, _____, processing, and distribution.
e: The main stages of metal recycling are collection, sorting, processing, and distribution.

q: During the sorting stage of metal recycling, scrap metals are separated according to their _____.
e: Scrap metals are separated according to their types.

q: The processing stage of metal recycling involves a series of mechanical and _____ operations.
e: A series of mechanical and chemical operations is performed.

q: In the recycling of aluminium, purification is considered a _____ operation.
e: Purification is a chemical operation (mostly electrolysis) to be free from contaminants.

q: Metal recycling is beneficial to the environment by reducing mining operations, reducing air and water pollution, and conserving limited _____ reserves.
e: Recycling conserves limited fossil fuel reserves.

q: Potash alum ($K_2SO_4 \cdot Al_2(SO_4)_3 \cdot 24H_2O$) can be used in water purification, leather tanning and _____.
e: Potash alum can be used in water purification, leather tanning and dyeing.

q: Lead(II,IV) oxide (Red lead, $Pb_3O_4$) can be used for _____.
e: Lead(II,IV) oxide (Red lead, $Pb_3O_4$) can be used for surface coating.

q: Bordeaux mixture, a suspension of copper(II) sulphate ($CuSO_4$) and calcium hydroxide ($Ca(OH)_2$), is used to control _____ on grapes, melons and other berries.
e: Bordeaux mixture is used to control fungus on grapes, melons and other berries.

q: Brass finds uses in jewellery, machine bearings, electrical connections, door and _____.
e: Brass finds uses in jewellery, machine bearings, electrical connections, door and furniture.

q: Bronze is widely used in castings and _____ parts.
e: Bronze is widely used in castings and machine parts.

q: Stainless steel is hard and rustproof. This is used for cutlery and equipment in _____ factories.
e: Stainless steel is used for cutlery and equipment in chemical factories.
